rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Exercise headers pass the build-squint test.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm this rule guards: a cold reader squinting at JUST the headers (nav rail / index) should reconstruct what the exercise BUILDS. This exercise's own stated deliverable (L11 'What you build: a diagram of the work that recurs across your stack') is never named by H1 'Read your stack', which names the PROCESS (reading history) rather than the artifact. Comparative corpus check: the cited exemplar's actual H1 is `# Diagnose and *package*` (not 'diagnose-and-resend' as the filename suggests) — process verb paired with an italicized deliverable-noun. The same pattern recurs across the library: `Compound and *close the loop*`, `Exercise: *Audit* your agent`, `Build your challenge *memory*`, `Fork the worktree, *carry the evidence*`, `Map the access surface, own the *delta*`, `Codify the rules, place the file`. 'Read your stack' pairs the process verb with the SOURCE being read ('your stack'), not the output, which is the shape this rule bans outside the drill carve-out — and this isn't a drill (an artifact exists per L11). Not filing blocking: the title is still distinctive and searchable, and a prior writing pass on this same unchanged H1 read it as compliant; this is a genuine disagreement on a judgement call, not a mechanical miss.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Name the artifact rather than the input, e.g. `Read your stack, *draw the shape*` or `Map the work you repeat` — title rename is cheap; the file's slug (`read-your-stack.md`) is a separate, costlier graph op per the rule's own note and needn't move with it.
